name: SpreadsheetBench
intro: SpreadsheetBench是一个具有挑战性的电子表格操作基准，完全来源于真实世界的场景，旨在让当前的大型语言模型（LLMs）沉浸在电子表格用户的实际工作流程中。与依赖合成查询和简化电子表格文件的现有基准不同，SpreadsheetBench由从在线Excel论坛收集的912个真实问题构建而成，这些问题反映了用户错综复杂的需求。相关的电子表格包含多种表格数据，如多表、非标准关系表和丰富的非文本元素。此外，我们提出了一种更可靠的评估指标，类似于在线评测平台，为每个指令创建多个电子表格文件作为测试用例，确保评估能够处理不同值的电子表格的鲁棒解决方案。我们对各种LLMs在单轮和多轮推理设置下的综合评估揭示了最先进（SOTA）模型与人类表现之间存在巨大差距，突显了基准的难度。
org: Renmin University of China, Tsinghua University
build_method: 真实论坛采集, GPT-4改写, 专家标注, 多测试用例构造
eval_feature: 真实世界场景, 每题多测试用例, 单轮与多轮
build_method_en: Real-forum collection, GPT-4 rewriting, expert annotation, multi-case construction
eval_feature_en: Real-world scenarios, Multiple test cases per instruction, Single- and multi-round
intro_en: SpreadsheetBench is a challenging spreadsheet operation benchmark entirely derived from real-world scenarios, designed to immerse current large language models (LLMs) in the actual workflows of spreadsheet users. Unlike existing benchmarks that rely on synthetic queries and simplified spreadsheet files, SpreadsheetBench is built from 912 real questions collected from online Excel forums, reflecting users' complex needs. The associated spreadsheets contain diverse tabular data, including multi-sheet, non-standard relational tables, and rich non-text elements. Additionally, we propose a more reliable evaluation metric, similar to online testing platforms, by creating multiple spreadsheet files as test cases for each instruction to ensure the assessment can handle robust solutions across spreadsheets with varying values. Our comprehensive evaluation of various LLMs under single-turn and multi-turn reasoning settings reveals a significant gap between state-of-the-art (SOTA) models and human performance, highlighting the benchmark’s difficulty.

drawio_review_note: Aligned with SpreadsheetBench arXiv:2406.14991 Sections 2.1-2.4 and Appendix B; official RUCKBReasoning/SpreadsheetBench repository. SpreadsheetBench starts from real spreadsheet-manipulation posts on ExcelForum, Chandoo, MrExcel, and ExcelGuru. The authors retain solved, software-independent, feasible, testable, and representative questions with spreadsheet attachments. GPT-4 rewrites scattered forum threads into self-contained instructions, which annotators verify; annotators also identify forum solutions, apply formulas or VBA, and specify cell- or sheet-level answer positions. Each suitable instruction receives the original input-output spreadsheet plus two data-modified corner-case test pairs. Rewritten questions, changed spreadsheet values, and shifted answer positions mitigate leakage. Twenty Excel specialists annotate; two validators and two authors perform two quality rounds. The release has 912 instructions and 2,729 test cases. A model generates one code solution per instruction, which is applied to every associated spreadsheet. Exact output matches are accepted. Soft OJ scoring grants per-test partial credit, while hard OJ scoring requires every test to pass; single- and up-to-five-round inference settings are evaluated.
